clue.text: Seducer's short length hair too wavy

definitions.note: read as 'Seducer is', the possessive standing for the verb

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for length

indicators.note: wavy hair is not straight, so these letters are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: A womaniser has sported a short, wavy hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hair' plays on the seducer's grooming, but 'wavy' only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, the rake in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, became a byword for a man who seduces women.

clue.text: Tube weapon shifted below to smother radio signal

indicators.note: to smother is to cover something over, so one piece wraps round the other
shifted letters are moved around, so the word below is rearranged

parts.note: a pip is a short beep, as in the time signal on the radio

explanation.surface: A weapon moved lower down is used to jam a radio transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' signals the rearrangement and 'to smother' the wrapping; PIP is the radio time beep.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which darts are shot by breath, a hunting weapon.

clue.text: One unknown to get into firm danger

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: firm means hard, solid
A is one, as in a single item
Z is an unknown in algebra, like x and y

explanation.surface: A single mystery outsider joins a company that is in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a risk or source of peril, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: See 23 across
Measure up cats and dogs?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned round

parts.note: cats and dogs are typical household pets

explanation.surface: Is it raining cats and dogs enough to take a reading?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' tempts as rain, but here it means pets; 'up' turns that word over.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken, as in 'take steps', and also a unit of pace.

clue.text: Conspicuous person calling for taxi's public announcement device

parts.note: loud can mean showy or conspicuous, as with garish clothes
one who hails a cab is a hailer

explanation.surface: A showy person flagging down a cab has a loud announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone-type amplifier used to address crowds is called by this name.

clue.text: Braying beast making a fool of a woman

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A donkey's braying makes a woman look silly.
explanation.definitionFit: A female donkey, an animal known for its braying call.

clue.text: Ex-Chancellor, Rod, turned independent — vegetable!

parts.note: Helmut Kohl was Chancellor of Germany

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word for rod runs backwards

parts.note: a bar is a rod

explanation.surface: A former head of government and a man named Rod changed allegiance to stand alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a turnip-like cabbage grown for its swollen stem, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Sound of trumpeter with hot mouthpiece

parts.note: a trumpet gives a toot
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A trumpet player's sound with a heated mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthpiece' looks like part of the trumpet, but it means a piece of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a piece of the mouth, a tooth fits this playful wording.

clue.text: See 26 down
Diametrically opposite pointed rocks, one follows source of Amazon

indicators.note: following means coming after, so these letters are placed behind
the source of a river is its beginning, so the first letter is taken
something that rocks is shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article meaning one

explanation.surface: Sharp stones lie downstream from where the Amazon rises, a world away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun beside 'pointed' but is the anagram signal; 'source of' takes just the opening letter of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes places on the opposite side of the globe, directly opposite in position.

clue.text: Powdered bottom

definitions.meaning: milled into powder, as coffee or pepper is
the floor or earth at the base of something

explanation.definitionFit: Ground is both the past participle of grind and the earth or base beneath us.

clue.text: Don't think much of unfairly breaking V&A nude rule

indicators.note: breaking a rule unfairly smashes it up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, giving V and A

explanation.surface: A statue in the London museum flouts the rule against nudity.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert, a London museum of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: To undervalue something is to underrate it, to hold it in too low regard.

clue.text: Run over, note, by late person's vehicle

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a hearse carries the dead, the 'late'

explanation.surface: Run down by a funeral car, with a memo taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' looks like a road accident, nicely backed by the hearse, but it means practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play or speech is to go through it again, practising it.

clue.text: What did you say about bacon end being dear in Scotland?

indicators.note: turning about means facing round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: eh? asks someone to repeat themselves

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a repeat when talk turns to the last of the bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots and northern English, hen is an affectionate address to a woman, like 'love'.

clue.text: Party, one way and another, has awful things one's unable to name

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the word for party is read forwards one way, then backwards the other

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: awful means bad, so the letters come out disordered

explanation.surface: A celebration, seen from every angle, includes dreadful items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way and another' gives DO then OD; 'awful' makes AHS from HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodahs are thingummies, words used for objects whose names escape you.

clue.text: Fruit article located between dimensions

indicators.note: being located between means sitting in the middle, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: height and width are dimensions, abbreviated H and W
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of produce sits between measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: A haw is the red berry of the hawthorn shrub.

clue.text: Everlasting event being so even

definitions.meaning: going on for ever, without cease
the word event with its last letter dropped becomes even, so being thus treated it is without its finish

explanation.surface: An eternal happening stays balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: take the word 'event', make it lack its end (T) and it reads 'even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means everlasting, and literally means without an end.

clue.text: Livestock cleanser moved deep inside boat

indicators.note: inside means within, so these letters go into the other word

parts.note: a ship is a boat

indicators.note: moved letters are shifted around, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaning wash for animals is shifted deep into the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' signals the rearrangement and 'inside' the insertion; a sheep dip is also the trough itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dip is the insecticidal liquid in which flocks are plunged to clean them.

clue.text: Scare about energy needed for goods on the move

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for scare surrounds the other letter

parts.note: a fright is a scare
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Alarm surrounds the power demands of shifting cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo carried by lorry, ship or train, goods in transit.

clue.text: Blend or brew or fictional small family member?

indicators.note: to blend is to mix, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Mix a drink or two for a member of a tiny storybook family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borrowers, Mary Norton's children's books, are a family of tiny people living under floorboards.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tiny person in Mary Norton's novels is one of the Borrowers clan.

clue.text: See 23 across
Bothersome if I ratify novel written by a suitably connected 5 15 17 25

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Approving an irritating new book by a famous scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Join the answers to 5, 15, 17 and 25 down (STEP, HEN, HAW, KING) and you get Stephen Hawking, author of this book.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Hawking's popular cosmology book is the one this joined-up name wrote.

clue.text: Ancient, say, going north, constrained by unstable load

indicators.note: being constrained by something means being held within it, so these letters go inside
an unstable load shifts, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, going north means travelling upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Something ancient, for instance, heading north under a wobbly cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' works only because this is a down entry; 'unstable' signals the anagram and 'constrained by' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means having existed for a very long time, of great antiquity.

clue.text: Sherwood's first wood cutter's consumer aid

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: teak is a hardwood
a knife is a cutter; the possessive gives no letter

explanation.surface: A lumberjack from Sherwood Forest helps out shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' here means one who eats, not a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as aiding an eater, a steak knife is a utensil helping one consume meat.

clue.text: Best selling writer's weight reduced (eating short measure)

definitions.note: read as 'writer is', the possessive standing for the verb

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: kg is the shortened form of kilogram, a weight
in is the abbreviation for inch, a measure

explanation.surface: A popular author has slimmed down despite eating a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen King writes bestselling horror novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King, the horror novelist, is among the world's top-selling authors.

clue.text: See 2
Old-fashioned titillation in the butler's view?

definitions.meaning: a coin-operated machine ... saucy pictures, an old-style seaside amusement
a butler stooping at a keyhole gets a sneaky glimpse

explanation.definitionFit: A peep show is a saucy viewing box, and literally a spying glimpse.

clue.text: Keen to do so noisily

parts.note: to keen is to wail for the dead, so the clue says keening is lamenting loudly

explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to lament, so the answer is grieving, done loudly in a keen.

clue.text: Greek fetching Trojan having left one cold

indicators.note: having means holding within, so the letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Helen of Troy lived in the city as Paris's wife
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Greek brings a Trojan who left one out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen of Troy was herself Greek, which makes the wordplay apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenic means of Greece or the Greek people.
